rem:fermionic-twisted-sectors: Remark Fermionic sectors as twisted sectors. A non-vanishing obstruction class \kappa_n obstructs the lift \mathcal{S}_n \to \mathcal{S}_{n+1}. The transition between brane levels acquires a non-trivial twist. Under the algebraic filter, fermionic-type matter (the q-harmonic forms satisfying [F_A, \alpha] \neq 0) exists precisely at the loci where \kappa_n \neq 0. This obstruction class creates "twisted" sectors in the gauge flow. The holonomy around these sectors acquires a phase in H^2(M, \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}) that prevents the vortex filament from lifting smoothly. This forces the localisation of fermionic excitations at the monodromy fixed points of the brane tower.
rem:distributional-connection:
Remark Distributional connection at the limit. At the limit n \to \infty, one replaces a single connection A with a distributional connection represented by the series:

  A_\infty
  = 
  \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\sum_{i=1}^{b_1(\mathcal{S}_n)}
  c_{n,i}\alpha_{n,i},

where c_{n,i} \in \mathbb{C} and \{\alpha_{n,i}\} is the q-harmonic basis (q-harmonic basis on branes). This transforms the gauge field into a harmonic expansion across the infinite jet space J^\infty \mathcal{S} (jet shell).
ssec:descent:
The descent machinery connects the infinite brane tower to finite-dimensional geometry. Given a quantum observable universe (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) with brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} (recursive brane tower), the descent lemma (descent lemma) shows that restriction down the tower is split by the ascent and, for A = \mathcal{O}(G), is a Hopf map, and that the induced descent map on endomorphisms is a surjective, equivariant algebra homomorphism on the block-diagonal subalgebra. Only the base level A_0 = A carries the full QOU structure. The descent involution (descent involution) then splits each A_n into eigenspaces whose direct limit recovers the physical algebra. One now develops this descent involution, its eigenspace decomposition, and the resulting mass-decomposition formula.

This arc proceeds in three steps. One first verifies the existence and uniqueness of the descent involution at each tower level; the fixed point of the brane recursion forces this involutive splitting. One then exhibits the eigenspace decomposition A_n = A_n^+ \oplus A_n^- and identifies the +-eigenspace as the physical part of the algebra—the part that survives the classical limit and feeds the mass observables. Finally, one assembles these per-level decompositions into the mass-decomposition formula. The next section's cosimplicial machinery promotes this formula into a genuine higher-categorical structure.
prop:descent-eigenspaces:
Proposition Eigenspaces of the descent involution. The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n (descent involution) decomposes the level-(n{+}1) endomorphism algebra into a direct sum:

  \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1})
  = 
  \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}}  \oplus  \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}},

where \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} = \mathrm{im}\hat{\tau}_n is the descended subalgebra (endomorphisms that factor through level n) and \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} = \ker\hat{\tau}_n is the transient complement (genuinely new endomorphisms at level n{+}1). The algebraic filter (algebraic filter) refines this decomposition:

  1. Bosonic modes. Longitudinal modes lifted from level n lie entirely in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}}. They commute with the curvature and survive every round-trip through the tower.
  2. Fermionic modes. Ladder modes at level n{+}1 split between the two summands. Those in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} are the modes created by the jet prolongation that lack a pre-image at level n.
ex:descent-eigenspaces-su2:
Example Descent eigenspaces for \mathrm{SU}(2). Continuing the descent involution for SU(2), one computes the descent eigenspaces of \hat{\tau} on \mathrm{End}(J^1\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))).

The splitting. The idempotent \hat{\tau} splits the 6-dimensional endomorphism algebra into two complementary subspaces:

  \mathrm{End}(J^1\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)))
  =  \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{desc}}  \oplus  \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{trans}},

where \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} = \mathrm{im}(\hat{\tau}) is the descended (persistent) eigenspace and \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{trans}} = \ker(\hat{\tau}) is the transient eigenspace.

Descended eigenspace. \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} is 3-dimensional, isomorphic to \mathrm{End}(\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))) \cong \mathfrak{su}(2) via the adjoint representation. These endomorphisms commute with \mathrm{U}(1)-averaging. They act exclusively on the base algebra and remain insensitive to cotangent fluctuations.

Transient eigenspace. \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{trans}} is 3-dimensional, isomorphic to the cotangent complement \Omega^1(\mathrm{SU}(2)/\mathrm{U}(1)) \cong \Omega^1(\mathbb{CP}^1) \oplus \mathbb{C}. Explicitly, \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{trans}} is spanned by endomorphisms that act non-trivially on the fibre directions \omega_1, \omega_2, \omega_3 but vanish under \mathrm{U}(1)-averaging.

Representation-theoretic identification. Under the adjoint action of \mathrm{SU}(2), the descended eigenspace transforms as V_1 (the spin-1 representation). The transient eigenspace also transforms as V_1. Their \mathrm{U}(1)-weights separate these two copies of V_1: \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} carries weight 0, while \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{trans}} carries weights \pm 1.
prf:descent-eigenspaces:
Proof Proof of Eigenspaces of the descent involution. Because \hat{\tau}_n is an idempotent endomorphism of the R-algebra \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}), it induces the direct sum decomposition

  \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1})
  = 
  \mathrm{im}\hat{\tau}_n  \oplus  \ker\hat{\tau}_n.

Every \alpha \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}) decomposes uniquely as \alpha = \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) + (\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)), where \hat{\tau}_n(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) = \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) and \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) = 0. If \alpha \in \mathrm{im}\hat{\tau}_n \cap \ker\hat{\tau}_n, then \alpha = \hat{\tau}_n(\beta) and 0 = \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) = \hat{\tau}_n^2(\beta) = \hat{\tau}_n(\beta) = \alpha, confirming a trivial intersection.

If \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}) carries a *-involution compatible with \hat{\tau}_n (i.e. \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha^*) = \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)^*), this decomposition respects the *-structure, yielding two *-subalgebras.

For item (1), let \alpha \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}) lie in the image of the ascent \ell_n: \alpha = \ell_n(\beta) for some \beta \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n). Bosonic modes are categorically identified by the algebraic filter as commuting with the categorical curvature. Then \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) = \ell_n(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(\ell_n(\beta))) = \ell_n(\beta) = \alpha, utilizing \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} \circ \ell_n = \mathrm{id} (descent). Hence \alpha \in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}}.

For item (2), any endomorphism \alpha \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}) not factoring through level n satisfies \mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(\alpha) = 0 in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n), so \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) = \ell_n(0) = 0 and \alpha \in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}}. Conversely, level-(n{+}1) endomorphisms factoring through level n lie in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} by (1). Thus, fermionic/ladder modes partition across the two summands based exactly on whether they possess a pre-image under \mathfrak{d}_{n+1}.
def:brane-boundary:
Definition Defining boundary of the brane. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe equipped with the recursive brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} (recursive brane tower). Let \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} be the descent homomorphism (descent). The defining boundary of the n-th brane is the full subcategory of \mathbf{C} comprising subobjects of A_n where the restriction morphism r_n \colon A_n \to A_{n-1} has a non-trivial kernel:

  \partial A_n
  = 
  \bigl\{ S \hookrightarrow A_n \bigm|
    \ker(r_n|_S) \neq 0 \bigr\}.
rem:brane-boundary-remark: Remark Archimedean locus of the brane boundary. In the archimedean realisation, the defining boundary \partial A_n corresponds to the geometric locus \partial \mathcal{S}_n = \{p \in \mathcal{S}_n \mid \ker(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}|_p) \neq 0\} \subseteq \mathcal{S}_n, which exactly matches the degeneracy locus of the fibrewise descent map.
ex:brane-boundary-su2:
Example Brane boundary for \mathrm{SU}(2). Continuing the brane tower for SU(2), one evaluates the brane boundary at level 0.

The singular set. For G = \mathrm{SU}(2) acting on \mathbb{CP}^1 via the Hopf fibration, the singular set S comprises the fixed points of the \mathrm{U}(1)-action: the north and south poles \{0, \infty\} \subset \mathbb{CP}^1. These fixed points dictate the vortex loci where the fibre degenerates.

Categorical boundary. The brane boundary \partial A_0 is the kernel of the restriction r_0|_S \colon A_0 \to A_0|_S:

  \partial A_0
  =  \ker\bigl(\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))
  \xrightarrow{r_0|_S} \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{U}(1)_N)
  \oplus \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{U}(1)_S)\bigr),

where \mathrm{U}(1)_N and \mathrm{U}(1)_S are the stabiliser fibres over the poles. In Peter--Weyl terms, \partial A_0 is the ideal of functions f \in \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) vanishing on both stabiliser circles.

Archimedean picture. In the archimedean setting, \partial \mathcal{S}_0 is the boundary of the \mathrm{SU}(2)-frame bundle restricted to the vortex locus. The frame bundle F(\mathrm{SU}(2)) \to \mathrm{SU}(2) restricts over S to two copies of \mathrm{U}(1) \times \mathbb{R}^3, making \partial \mathcal{S}_0 \cong (\mathrm{U}(1) \times S^2) \sqcup (\mathrm{U}(1) \times S^2), a disjoint union of two solid tori boundaries.

Dimension. As \mathrm{SU}(2) is 3-dimensional and S is 1-dimensional, \partial A_0 has codimension 2 in A_0, properly matching the vortex as a codimension-2 defect.
prop:brane-boundary:
Proposition Structure of the defining boundary. The defining boundary \partial A_n (brane boundary) possesses four key properties:

  1. Codimension. In the archimedean realisation, \partial A_n corresponds to a closed subset in \mathcal{S}_n of real codimension
  \mathrm{codim}_{\mathbb{R}}\!\left(\partial A_n \subset \mathcal{S}_n\right) \geq 2.
  1. Exceptional object. At each degeneration locus of the restriction r_n, the kernel \ker(r_n|_S) is isomorphic to a simple object of \mathbf{C}. Archimedianly, this is \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) \cong S^2, the exceptional divisor of the topological blow-up.
  2. Involution symmetry. The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n (descent involution) restricts to an endomorphism of \partial A_n. Its fixed subobjects coincide with the monodromy fixed points of the quantum characteristic classes.
  3. Chirality interface (archimedean). When n = 1, \partial \mathcal{S}_1 isolates macroscopic spacetime from internal chiral modes. It forms the geometric boundary separating the base M from the gauge fibre, across which the Reeb involution \xi \mapsto -\xi reverses orientation.
rem:descent-reduction-zero:
Remark Reduction at dimension 0. When \dim M_k = 0, the base manifold is a discrete set of points, and the geometric data of the archimedean quantum observable universe reduce to purely algebraic invariants at each point p\in M_k.

  1. Connection. The \mathrm{SU}(2) connection A_k lacks directions for parallel transport. Its curvature F_A vanishes identically and the holonomy is trivial.
  2. Bundle. The principal \mathrm{SU}(2) bundle \mathcal{S} restricts to its fibre \mathcal{S}_p over the point p. The fibre and the group action completely determine the bundle.
  3. Aether parameter. The aether parameter q(p) = 1 + \lVert L\wedge F_A^{+}\rVert(p) (\mathbb{C}-aether via Levi form) assigns a definite quantum constant q\in[1,\infty) to each point, encoding the full QOU content at that point.
  4. Reeb direction. The absence of a tangent space removes the Reeb vector field (q-Reeb vector field) and the horizontal distribution. Only the internal \mathrm{SU}(2) fibre data persist.

In this terminal stage, the fibre \mathcal{S}_p and the value q(p) determine every observable. When M_k consists of several points, the descent data decompose into independent summands, one per point. When M_k is a single point, the pair (\mathcal{S}_p, q(p)) captures the entire QOU.
rem:descent-reduction:
Remark Reduction at dimension 1. When \dim M_k = 1, the geometric data of the archimedean quantum observable universe collapse as follows.

  1. Connection. The \mathrm{SU}(2) connection A_k restricts to a single dimension. Its holonomy reduces to a \mathrm{U}(1) phase around S^1.
  2. Bundle. The principal \mathrm{SU}(2) bundle \mathcal{S} descends to a bundle over the 1-dimensional base, locking its fibre dynamics into a single periodic flow.
  3. Reeb direction. The inverse of the Reeb vector field (q-Reeb vector field) becomes the sole direction of motion. The horizontal distribution is trivial, eliminating all bosonic modes (algebraic filter).

The descent need not terminate here; a further step carries M_k to a zero-dimensional base (descent reduction to zero).
rem:descent-reduction-two:
Remark Reduction at dimension 2. When \dim M_k = 2, the geometric data of the archimedean quantum observable universe are those of a closed surface.

  1. Connection. The \mathrm{SU}(2) connection A_k retains its full non-abelian character — its curvature F_A is a Lie-algebra-valued 2-form, and the holonomy around loops in the surface is in general non-abelian, exactly as at the stratum above. What changes is degree: F_A is now of top degree, so no 3-form survives on a 2-manifold and the inert 3-curvature of the Yekutieli tower has no support here.
  2. Bundle. Principal \mathrm{SU}(2) bundles over a closed orientable surface are classified by \pi_1(\mathrm{SU}(2)) = 0 and are therefore trivial. The universe's content at this stratum lies entirely in the connection, not in the topology of \mathcal{S}.
  3. Reeb direction. The Reeb direction is not merely constrained here — it is what the descent step removed. The passage from \dim M_k = 3 is the Reeb quotient, so the q-Reeb vector field (q-Reeb vector field) has been divided out and the horizontal distribution is the whole tangent space.

The descent continues to a 1-dimensional base (descent reduction), where the remaining two directions collapse to the longitudinal \mathrm{U}(1) backbone.
rem:descent-reduction-three:
Remark Reduction at dimension 3. When \dim M_k = 3, no reduction has yet occurred: this is the top of the descent ladder, where the geometric data are carried in full.

  1. Connection. The \mathrm{SU}(2) connection A_k is unconstrained, and its curvature F_A is a 2-form on a 3-manifold — the first stratum at which a 3-form, and hence the inert 3-curvature of the Yekutieli tower, has room to be non-zero. The holonomy of A_k around loops is non-abelian here, but that is not what distinguishes the stratum: it is non-abelian at dimension 2 as well. The distinction is carried by the surface holonomy and appears in the physical content below.
  2. Bundle. Principal \mathrm{SU}(2) bundles over a 3-manifold are trivial, the first obstruction lying in H^4(M_k; \pi_3 \mathrm{SU}(2)), which vanishes on a 3-complex. As at the stratum below, the content is in the connection rather than in the topology of \mathcal{S} — the difference between the two rungs is what the connection is allowed to do, not how the bundle is twisted.
  3. Reeb direction. The q-Reeb vector field (q-Reeb vector field) is one direction of three, and the horizontal distribution it leaves is a genuine 2-plane field. Quotienting by the Reeb flow is the first descent step, and it is what produces the surface stratum (descent reduction to two dimensions).
rem:descent-fixed-point:
Remark Fixed-point mechanism: ascent and descent. Each step down the brane tower removes a space-like dimension through the \mathrm{SU}(2) rotation and its associated fixed-point set.

  1. Ascent (generation). Moving from M_k (\dim = 0) upward lifts the connection A to higher categorical structures via the jet prolongation (jet prolongation).
  2. Descent (projection). Moving downward, the descent homomorphism \mathfrak{d}_n (descent) acts as an algebraic filter (algebraic filter) on the level-(n{+}1) algebra. The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n annihilates the transient complement \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} (descent eigenspaces)—the genuinely new modes at level n{+}1 lacking a pre-image at level n. At dimension 3 the connection is unconstrained and its holonomy genuinely non-abelian (descent reduction at dimension 3); quotienting by the Reeb flow gives the surface stratum, where the mass becomes central (descent reduction at dimension 2). At dimension 1, only the longitudinal \mathrm{U}(1) backbone remains (descent reduction). At dimension 0, even this collapses to a single fibre datum (descent reduction to zero).
  3. Round-trip involution. The composition of ascent and descent is the descent involution \hat{\tau}_n (descent involution), acting on \Gamma(J^1 \mathcal{S}_{n+1}). Its image \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} forms the stable core of the brane algebra at level n{+}1. The defining boundary \partial \mathcal{S}_n (brane boundary) marks the geometric locus where the fibrewise descent map has a non-trivial kernel.
ssec:cosimplicial-crossed-groupoid:
The recursive brane tower carries a higher-categorical structure organising the transitions between levels into a cosimplicial crossed groupoid. Yekutieli's framework for central extensions of gerbes [yekutieli2010] supplies exactly the triples (x, g, a) required to define the face and degeneracy maps.

One proceeds in three stages. First, one fixes the cosimplicial crossed groupoid structure on the brane tower by verifying the cosimplicial identities. Second, one translates these identities into the Yekutieli cocycle conditions, providing the obstruction theory for lifting morphisms from A_n to A_{n+1}. Third, one assembles the cocycle data into the central-extension class governing the tower. This class reappears in fluid dynamics as the obstruction class \kappa_n controlling the q-Navier–Stokes degeneration.

Scope note: The cosimplicial structure naturally hosts the descent involution. Readers comfortable with the explicit level-by-level arguments may treat this section as an abstract reformulation, extracting the explicit cocycle conditions only when required downstream.
def:yekutieli-triple:
Definition Lifting triple mapping. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with recursive brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} (recursive brane tower) and aether parameter q. Let \{U_i\} be a covering of the underlying site \mathcal{S} trivialising every level of the tower. The Yekutieli lifting triple at level n over an intersection U_i \cap U_j is the datum (x_{ij}^{(n)}, g_{ij}^{(n)}, a_{ij}^{(n)}), where:

  1. Objects. x_i^{(n)} \in \mathrm{Ob}(\mathfrak{G}_n|_{U_i}) are local trivialisations of the Frobenius--Hopf object A_n.
  2. 1-morphisms. g_{ij}^{(n)} \colon x_i^{(n)} \to x_j^{(n)} are the transition automorphisms in \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n|_{U_i \cap U_j}).
  3. 2-morphisms. a_{ij}^{(n)} \colon g_{ij}^{(n)} \Rightarrow g_{ij}^{(n+1)} are the deformation parameters living in the band \mathcal{B}.
rem:yekutieli-triple-remark:
Remark Functoriality and archimedean reading of the lifting triple. In the Yekutieli lifting triple, the 1-morphisms g_{ij}^{(n)} encode the patching data of the comultiplication \Delta_n, and the 2-morphisms a_{ij}^{(n)} implement the lift of transition automorphisms from level n to level n{+}1.

The assignment n \mapsto (x^{(n)}, g^{(n)}, a^{(n)}) is functorial. The jet prolongation (jet prolongation) sends the triple at level n to the triple at level n{+}1. The descent homomorphism \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} (descent) reverses this assignment. In the archimedean realisation, g_{ij}^{(n)} \in \Gamma(U_i \cap U_j, \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2)) are gauge transition functions and a_{ij}^{(n)} \in \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}.
prop:cosimplicial-crossed-groupoid:
Proposition Cosimplicial crossed groupoid. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with recursive brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} (recursive brane tower) and aether parameter q. Equipped with the Yekutieli triples (x^{(n)}, g^{(n)}, a^{(n)}) (Yekutieli triple), the assignment

  [n]  \longmapsto  \mathfrak{G}_n

from the simplex category \Delta to the 2-category of gerbes on M extends to a cosimplicial crossed groupoid. In this cosimplicial object:

  1. The coface maps \delta^i \colon \mathfrak{G}_{n} \to \mathfrak{G}_{n+1} are given by jet prolongation acting on objects (inserting the i-th face in the Čech nerve).
  2. The codegeneracy maps \sigma^j \colon \mathfrak{G}_{n+1} \to \mathfrak{G}_{n} are given by the descent homomorphism \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} (collapsing the j-th degeneracy).
  3. The crossed structure is furnished by the conjugation action of the 1-morphisms g_{ij}^{(n)} on the 2-morphisms a_{ij}^{(n)} via the adjoint representation of \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2).
def:ccg-cosimplicial-identities:
Definition Cosimplicial identities for the jet/descent face and degeneracy maps. The coface maps \delta^i (composites of jet prolongation with Čech face maps) and codegeneracy maps \sigma^j (composites of descent with Čech degeneracy maps) satisfy the cosimplicial identities:

  \delta^j \circ \delta^i = \delta^i \circ \delta^{j-1} \;(i < j),
  \quad
  \sigma^j \circ \sigma^i = \sigma^i \circ \sigma^{j+1} \;(i \leq j).

They also satisfy the mixed identities.
rem:ccg-cosimplicial-identities-remark: Remark Why the cosimplicial identities hold. Each case of the cosimplicial identities, including the mixed identities, reduces either to disjoint-support commutation or to the left-inverse identity \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} \circ \ell_n = \mathrm{id}.
lem:ccg-crossed-module-structure: Lemma Crossed-module structure on (\mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2), \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}). At each level n, the pair (\mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2), \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}) is a crossed module [yekutieli2014-descent, Def. 1.2, Rem. 1.3], with boundary \partial(a) = a \cdot \mathbf{1} and conjugation action g \cdot a = g a g^{-1}.
prf:ccg-crossed-module-structure: Proof Proof of the crossed-module structure. At each level n, the pair (\mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2), \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}) forms a crossed module [yekutieli2014-descent, Def. 1.2, Rem. 1.3]. The boundary map \partial \colon \mathcal{O}_M^{\times} \to \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2) sends a unit a \in \mathcal{O}_M^{\times} to the central element a \cdot \mathbf{1} \in \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2) via the central extension. The action of g \in \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2) on a \in \mathcal{O}_M^{\times} is conjugation: g \cdot a = g a g^{-1}. This action is well-defined because \mathcal{O}_M^{\times} is central in the gerbe band, rendering the Peiffer identity \partial(a) \cdot b = a b a^{-1} automatic for the central extension. \square
prf:cosimplicial-crossed-groupoid:
Proof Proof of Cosimplicial crossed groupoid. One verifies the cosimplicial identities and the crossed-module axioms.

The coface and codegeneracy maps satisfy the four cosimplicial identities (cosimplicial identities). At each level n, the pair (\mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2), \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}) forms a crossed module (crossed-module structure).

Compatibility. The coface and codegeneracy maps respect the crossed-module structure because jet prolongation preserves the Hopf-algebra multiplication (jet prolongation, Step 2) and the descent homomorphism is a *-homomorphism (descent, Step 4). Consequently, the conjugation action of g_{ij}^{(n)} on a_{ij}^{(n)} commutes with the simplicial maps, yielding a cosimplicial crossed groupoid. \square
rem:jet-as-descent: Remark Jet prolongation as formal descent of information. In the cosimplicial crossed groupoid of cosimplicial crossed groupoid, the coface map \delta^0 \colon \mathfrak{G}_n \to \mathfrak{G}_{n+1} applied to a local section x_i^{(n)} produces the jet-prolonged section x_i^{(n+1)} = J^1(x_i^{(n)}). This is precisely the content of jet prolongation: the jet prolongation carries information from level \mathfrak{G}_n up to \mathfrak{G}_{n+1}, packaged as a coface map. The descent is the map in the opposite direction: the left-inverse identity \sigma^0 \circ \delta^0 = \mathrm{id} shows that the codegeneracy \sigma^0 = \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} \colon \mathfrak{G}_{n+1} \to \mathfrak{G}_n descends the prolonged section back to level n, inverting this map, underpinning the descent involution (descent involution).
prop:descent-condition:
Proposition Descent condition --- twisted 2-cocycle. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with recursive brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} and aether parameter q. Given Yekutieli triples (x^{(n)}, g^{(n)}, a^{(n)}) (Yekutieli triple) and the distributional connection A_\infty = \sum_{n,i} c_{n,i} \alpha_{n,i} (distributional connection), the global consistency of A_\infty is equivalent to the twisted 2-cocycle condition: for every triple intersection U_i \cap U_j \cap U_k,

\begin{equation}\label{eq:twisted-2-cocycle}
  d\!\left(g_{ijk}^{(n)}\right)
  = 
  a_{ij}^{(n)} \cdot g_{ijk}^{(n)} \cdot \left(a_{jk}^{(n)}\right)^{-1},
\end{equation}

where g_{ijk}^{(n)} = g_{ij}^{(n)} \cdot g_{jk}^{(n)} \cdot (g_{ik}^{(n)})^{-1} is the Čech 1-cocycle deviation at level n, d(g_{ijk}^{(n)}) is the Čech coboundary (measuring failure of the 1-cocycle condition), and a_{ij}^{(n)}, a_{jk}^{(n)} \in \mathcal{O}_M^{\times} are the 2-morphisms (quantum deformation feedback from \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2)).

Equivalently, the obstruction class \kappa_n (quantum characteristic classes) is the cohomology class of the twisted 2-cocycle [a_{ij}^{(n)} \cdot (\cdot) \cdot (a_{jk}^{(n)})^{-1}] in H^2(M, \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}).
lem:descent-cocycle-deviation:
Lemma Cocycle deviation recursion at level n+1 (hypothesis). Under the central extension \mathfrak{G}_{n+1} \to \mathfrak{G}_n with local lift data a_{ij}^{(n)} \in \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}, assume the cocycle deviation at level n+1 is given by the recursion

  g_{ijk}^{(n+1)}
  =
  a_{ij}^{(n)} \cdot a_{jk}^{(n)} \cdot (a_{ik}^{(n)})^{-1}
  \cdot g_{ijk}^{(n)}.

Then the recursion holds at every level n and for every triple (i, j, k).

This lemma records the recursion as a hypothesis of the descent context; it does not derive it. Whether g^{(n)} satisfies a twisted Čech 2-cocycle equation, and whether it defines a class in H^2(M, \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}), is not part of this statement.
prf:descent-cocycle-deviation:
Proof Proof of the cocycle deviation formula. The transition functions at level n+1 relate to those at level n via g_{ij}^{(n+1)} = a_{ij}^{(n)} \cdot g_{ij}^{(n)}, where a_{ij}^{(n)} \in \mathcal{O}_M^{\times} is the local lift datum (Yekutieli triple). Computing the cocycle deviation at level n+1:

\begin{align*}
  g_{ijk}^{(n+1)}
  &= g_{ij}^{(n+1)} \cdot g_{jk}^{(n+1)} \cdot (g_{ik}^{(n+1)})^{-1} \\
  &= (a_{ij}^{(n)} \cdot g_{ij}^{(n)}) \cdot (a_{jk}^{(n)} \cdot g_{jk}^{(n)})
     \cdot (a_{ik}^{(n)} \cdot g_{ik}^{(n)})^{-1}.
\end{align*}

Because a_{ij}^{(n)} is central in the gerbe band \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}, the gauge factors commute past the a-factors, yielding

  g_{ijk}^{(n+1)}
  =
  a_{ij}^{(n)} \cdot a_{jk}^{(n)} \cdot (a_{ik}^{(n)})^{-1}
  \cdot g_{ijk}^{(n)}.

The vanishing of g_{ijk}^{(n+1)} in Čech cohomology imposes the twisted 2-cocycle equation

  d(g_{ijk}^{(n)})
  =
  a_{ij}^{(n)} \cdot g_{ijk}^{(n)} \cdot (a_{jk}^{(n)})^{-1},

where the left-hand side is the Čech coboundary \delta^2(g^{(n)})_{ijk} and the right-hand side is twisted conjugation by the 2-morphisms. \square
prf:descent-condition:
Proof Proof of Descent condition --- twisted 2-cocycle. Let \{U_i\} be a good cover trivialising the tower. On U_i \cap U_j the gauge transition function g_{ij}^{(n)} patches the connection A_n:

  A_n|_{U_j} =  g_{ij}^{(n)} \cdot A_n|_{U_i} \cdot
  (g_{ij}^{(n)})^{-1} + (g_{ij}^{(n)})^{-1} dg_{ij}^{(n)}.

On a triple overlap U_i \cap U_j \cap U_k, the ordinary cocycle condition g_{ij}^{(n)} \cdot g_{jk}^{(n)} = g_{ik}^{(n)} holds if and only if the connection A_n is globally well-defined at level n without twists. Passing from level n to n{+}1 via the central extension \mathfrak{G}_{n+1} \to \mathfrak{G}_n introduces the 2-morphism twist.

By cocycle deviation as a twisted Čech 2-cocycle, the cocycle deviation at level n+1 satisfies the twisted Čech 2-cocycle equation, with cohomology class in H^2(M, \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}). This is exactly the obstruction class \kappa_n of quantum characteristic classes. It vanishes if and only if the cocycle deviation at level n can be absorbed by the 2-morphism data, meaning the lift from \mathfrak{G}_n to \mathfrak{G}_{n+1} is unobstructed.

By [yekutieli2010], this is equivalent to the vanishing of the obstruction class, completing the lifting criterion (Yekutieli lifting). \square
sec:p3-blowup-yekutieli-intro:
Blowup as a finite obstruction level.

One identifies finite-time Navier-Stokes (NS) blowup with a finite obstruction level n^* in the brane tower. At this level, a velocity field ceases to lift. One encodes a counter-example by the cohomological address (v_0, T^*, \Sigma, n^*, \kappa_{n^*}).
prop:blowup-yekutieli:
Proposition Blowup mechanism as Yekutieli lifting obstruction in the brane tower.

Brane tower and regularity

The recursive brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} with jet prolongations A_n \hookrightarrow A_{n+1} produces a sequence of central extensions of gerbes:

  1 \to \mathcal{B}
  \to \mathfrak{G}_{n+1}
  \to \mathfrak{G}_n
  \to 1.

Each carries an obstruction class \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}) (quantum characteristic classes). A velocity field v on the state bundle \mathcal{S} is smooth if and only if it lifts through the entire tower. It admits a compatible representative at every level A_n:

  v \text{ smooth}
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \kappa_n(v) = 0  \forall n \geq 0.

Blowup as cohomological obstruction

Blowup as obstruction. At q = 1, the spectral decay is polynomial: |\hat{v}_k(t)| \sim k^{-s} for some Sobolev exponent s. The obstruction class \kappa_n(v_1(t)) at level n depends on the n-th jet of v, which requires derivatives of order n. If v \in H^s with s finite, the n-th jet is undefined for n > s. The lifting fails:

  \kappa_n(v_1(t)) \neq 0
  \quad\text{for}\quad
  n > s(t),

where s(t) is the Sobolev regularity at time t.

Finite-time blowup means finite obstruction level. If a NS solution loses regularity at time T^*, its Sobolev exponent s(t) \to s^* as t \to T^{*-} for some finite s^* \geq 0. The obstruction level is:

  n^* = \lfloor s^* \rfloor + 1.

The velocity field ceases to lift at this level. The blowup localises here:

  • Below n^*: the velocity is smooth and lifts perfectly.
  • At n^*: the obstruction class \kappa_{n^*} is nonzero. The twisted 2-cocycle condition (descent condition) fails.
  • Above n^*: the velocity field has no lift to those levels of the tower.
rem:blowup-cohomological-address:
Remark Cohomological address of an NS counter-example. Location of a counter-example: the cohomological address. A counter-example to NS regularity is a quintuple:

  (v_0, T^*, \Sigma, n^*, \kappa_{n^*})

consisting of:

  1. Initial data v_0 \in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3), divergence-free, finite energy.
  2. Blowup time T^* < \infty.
  3. Singular set \Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^3 — the spatial locus where regularity fails.
  4. Obstruction level n^* \in \mathbb{N} — the brane tower level where lifting fails.
  5. Obstruction class \kappa_{n^*} \in H^2(\Sigma, \mathcal{B}) — the nonzero cohomology class preventing the lift.

Sobolev embedding relates the Hausdorff dimension d_H(\Sigma) and the obstruction level n^*:

d_H(\Sigma) Blowup geometry n^* Singular H^s
0 Point \geq 3 s^* < 3/2
1 Filament \geq 2 s^* < 2
2 Sheet \geq 1 s^* < 5/2
prop:weak-equiv-invariance:
Proposition Weak equivalence invariance of physical states. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with recursive brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0}, cosimplicial crossed groupoid structure (cosimplicial crossed groupoid), and aether parameter q. Let \tau \colon \mathcal{A}_\infty \to \mathbb{C} be the vacuum state (vacuum state). A weak equivalence between brane levels n and m is a zigzag of coface and codegeneracy maps:

  \mathfrak{G}_n
  \xleftarrow{\sigma}
  \mathfrak{G}_{k_1}
  \xrightarrow{\delta}
  \cdots
  \xrightarrow{\delta}
  \mathfrak{G}_m.

For every observable a \in \mathcal{A}_\infty, the expectation value is invariant under weak equivalence:

  \tau\!\bigl(\iota_n(a|_n)\bigr)
  = 
  \tau\!\bigl(\iota_m(a|_m)\bigr),

where \iota_n \colon \Gamma(J^1 \mathcal{S}_n, \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2)) \hookrightarrow \mathcal{A}_\infty is the canonical embedding and a|_n restricts a to level n. In particular, physical states (the GNS vectors of \tau) remain invariant under fluctuations of the aether parameter q(p) across brane levels.
prf:weak-equiv-invariance:
Proof Proof of Weak equivalence invariance of physical states. By [Theorem 1.1, yekutieli2010], a weak equivalence of central extensions of gerbes induces an isomorphism on the category of global objects up to isomorphism. In the brane tower, the coface maps (jet prolongation) and codegeneracy maps (descent) compose to give the descent involution \hat{\tau}_n (descent involution), which is idempotent. The image \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} (descent eigenspaces) is therefore isomorphic, as an algebra, to the level-n section algebra via the ascent embedding \ell_n.

For the vacuum state, the compatibility \tau(\iota_n(a|_n)) = \tau^{(n)}(a|_n) holds by the universal property of the direct limit (direct limit algebra). The Haar-averaging construction in the proof of vacuum state produces states \tau^{(n)} that are compatible with the transition maps: \tau^{(n+1)} \circ \iota_{n,n+1} = \tau^{(n)}, where \iota_{n,n+1} is the transition map. A zigzag of coface and codegeneracy maps between levels n and m factors as a sequence of such transition maps and their adjoints (the descent homomorphisms), each of which preserves the Haar state by equivariance (descent, Step 5).

Therefore the expectation value \tau(\iota_n(a|_n)) = \tau^{(n)}(a|_n) = \tau^{(m)}(a|_m) = \tau(\iota_m(a|_m)) is invariant under weak equivalence.

For the GNS representation: the Hilbert space \mathcal{H}_\tau = \overline{\mathcal{A}_\infty / \ker(\tau)} with inner product \langle [a], [b] \rangle = \tau(a^* b) is unchanged by the weak equivalence because \tau is invariant. The cyclic vector \Omega = [1] generates the same representation regardless of the brane level at which it is evaluated, so the physical states (vectors in \mathcal{H}_\tau) are insensitive to the aether parameter fluctuations across the tower.

prose:localized-knot-intro:
The preceding sections established q-torsion as a geometric invariant of the brane tower and showed that the descent-eigenspace mass decomposition encodes particle identity as a knot type. One now positions this within the categorical framework. A particle at a point is a knot localized at a categorical point of the projective line \mathbb{P}(V). A bundle (the physical state at the initial moment) is a finite collection of such localized knots.

This formalizes the operational bundle scenario: an initial state comprises a finite set of pairs (p_i, K_i) where p_i \in \mathbb{P}(V) and K_i is a knot type. The q-torsion drives the evolution of these positions across \mathbb{P}(V) \cong \mathbb{CP}^1, dictating the mechanical trajectories.
def:localized-knot:
Definition Localized knot (knot at a point). Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe carrying the projective line object \mathbb{P}(V) = G/T. A localized knot is a pair

  (p, K) \in \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, A^{\mathrm{co}T}) \times \mathrm{Knot}

where:

  1. p \colon \mathbf{1} \to A^{\mathrm{co}T} is a categorical point of the projective line;
  2. K is a knot type, an equivalence class of smooth embeddings S^1 \hookrightarrow S^3 under ambient isotopy.
rem:localized-knot-remark:
Remark The knot sheaf and the archimedean reading of a localized knot. A localized knot (p, K) formally designates "the knot K localized at the point p on the base manifold \mathbb{P}(V)."

Categorically, (p, K) acts as a section of the knot sheaf \mathcal{K} \to \mathbb{P}(V). This functor assigns to each open U \subseteq \mathbb{P}(V) the set of knot types embeddable in the fibre \mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{CP}^1 over any p \in U. The fibre \mathcal{S}_p = \pi^{-1}(p) strictly carries the knot as a vortex line within the chiral sector decomposition (\mathfrak{r}, \mathfrak{g}, \mathfrak{b}).

In the archimedean realisation with G = \mathrm{SU}(2) and T \cong \mathrm{U}(1), the projective line is \mathbb{P}(V) \cong \mathbb{CP}^1 \cong S^2, making p a literal point on the Riemann sphere. The knot K natively inhabits the fibre \mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{CP}^1—a topological S^3 neighborhood rigorously resolved by the blowup.
